learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with specific knowledge of spatial geometry.
Introduce the student to the use of graphic software.
Train in the handling of industrial project drawings.

syllabus_topics: Manholes and other sewerage network elements.
Foundation, sanitation, and laying out plan.
Drawing and dimensioning of rolled profiles.
Floor plan of metal structure columns.
Slabs. One-way. Joists. Semi-joists. Two-way slabs.
Plumbing design. Cold water. Hot water.
Design and calculation of a sanitation network.
Introduction to the Autodesk Revit environment. Use of templates.
Introduction to parametric modeling. Parametric design of solids
Justification and methodology of the software used: Autodesk Inventor
Work environments: Operations environment. Assembly environment. Documentation environment. Presentations environment.
Drawing and detail views. Advanced annotation.
Creation of auxiliary views, cuts, sections, and other views.
Sheet metal parts. Plastic parts. Component and joint design

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment tasks for 'Applied Drawings' part (AE1)
Final CAD deliverable for 'Applied Drawings' part (AE2)
Continuous assessment tasks for '3D Parametric Drawing' part (AE4)
Computer-based test for '3D Parametric Drawing' part (AE5)
Challenge project for '3D Parametric Drawing' part (AE6)
Theoretical-practical exam for 'Applied Drawings' part (AE7) in global assessment
Practical computer-based exercise for '3D Parametric Drawing' part (AE8) in global assessment

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is the average of the 'Applied Drawings' part (Ncad) and the '3D Parametric Drawing' part (Ndp), provided each part is passed with a score of 5 or higher out of 10. Ncad is calculated as 0.4*AE1 + 0.35*AE2 + 0.25*AE3, where AE1 tasks are non-recoverable in the extraordinary session. Ndp is calculated as 0.2*AE4 + 0.5*AE5 + 0.3*AE6, where AE4 tasks and AE6 challenge are non-recoverable. In the extraordinary session, only recoverable activities of failed parts can be retaken, with the calculation method remaining identical. For global assessment, the 'Applied Drawings' part is 100% an exam (AE7), and the '3D Parametric Drawing' part is 100% a practical computer exercise (AE8); both parts must be passed with a minimum of 5/10, and the final grade is their arithmetic mean.
